claim: Arabidopsis thaliana is a small, annual dicotyledon of the Brassicaceae family and is the model of choice for developmental biology of higher plants.
source: Fulfilling all these criteria, Arabidopsis thaliana (Arabidopsis), a small, annual dicotyledon of the Brassicaceae family, is the model of choice for developmental biology of higher plants (Meyerowitz, 1989).
evidence: Supported by citation to Meyerowitz, 1989 and established scientific knowledge about Arabidopsis as a model organism.

claim: The meristematic and differentiation regions of the Arabidopsis root tip comprise 5-6 dozen cells in the radial dimension.
source: For example, while the meristematic and differentiation regions of the root tip comprise a mere 5–6 dozen cells in the radial dimension and can be imaged all across using state-of-the-art microscopes, cell number rapidly increases proximal, towards the mature root (Dolan et al., 1993).
evidence: Supported by citation to Dolan et al., 1993.

claim: The vascular cambium produces xylem tissues towards the inside and phloem tissues towards the outside.
source: The latter are produced by another cylindrical secondary meristem, the vascular cambium, which produces xylem tissues towards the inside and phloem tissues towards the outside (Nieminen et al., 2004; Groover and Robischon, 2006).
evidence: Supported by citations to Nieminen et al., 2004 and Groover and Robischon, 2006.

claim: Formation of xylem tissues through secondary growth is the main process of durable biomass accumulation in plants and most prominent in tree trunks.
source: Formation of xylem tissues through secondary growth is the main process of durable biomass accumulation in plants and most prominent in tree trunks (Groover and Robischon, 2006; Spicer and Groover, 2010).
evidence: Supported by citations to Groover and Robischon, 2006 and Spicer and Groover, 2010.

claim: Substantial secondary growth is observed in Arabidopsis hypocotyls.
source: In Arabidopsis, substantial secondary growth is not only observed at later stages of root development, but also in the hypocotyl, the embryonic stem (Chaffey et al., 2002; Sibout et al., 2008) (Figure 1A).
evidence: Supported by citations to Chaffey et al., 2002 and Sibout et al., 2008, and visual evidence in Figure 1A.

claim: The hypocotyl initiates secondary growth shortly after seedling establishment, once its cell elongation growth along the main body axis has ceased.
source: The hypocotyl initiates secondary growth shortly after seedling establishment, once its cell elongation growth along the main body axis has seized (Sibout et al., 2008; Ragni et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citations to Sibout et al., 2008 and Ragni et al., 2011.

claim: Secondary growth in the hypocotyl is not obscured by parallel elongation growth, making it an ideal model system for this process.
source: Thus, unlike in post-embryonic stems, secondary growth in the hypocotyl is not obscured by parallel elongation growth, making it an ideal model system for this process.
evidence: Based on logical inference from the comparison with post-embryonic stems.

claim: Hypocotyl secondary growth has two principal phases: an early phase of proportional growth and a later phase of xylem expansion.
source: Previous work has identified two principal phases of hypocotyl secondary growth, an early phase of proportional growth, when the cambium produces phloem and xylem tissues at roughly equal rates, and a later phase of xylem expansion, when the relative production of xylem dominates the radial expansion (Chaffey et al., 2002; Sibout et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by citations to Chaffey et al., 2002 and Sibout et al., 2008.

claim: Early phase xylem consists mainly of interconnected xylem vessels and xylem parenchyma cells.
source: Early phase xylem consists mainly of the interconnected xylem vessels (terminally differentiated, dead cells with perforated, thick cell walls that are the actual conducts for water and solutes) and xylem parenchyma cells.
evidence: Based on established knowledge of xylem tissue composition.

claim: Early phase phloem comprises sieve elements, companion cells, and phloem parenchyma cells.
source: Early phase phloem comprises the sieve elements (interconnected, enucleated but alive cells that perform the actual transport of the phloem sap), companion cells (which provide basic metabolism for sieve elements and are responsible for loading and un-loading of phloem sap cargo) and phloem parenchyma cells.
evidence: Based on established knowledge of phloem tissue composition.

claim: In the xylem expansion phase, both xylem and phloem start to differentiate fibers.
source: In the xylem expansion phase, both xylem and phloem also start to differentiate fibers (cells with thick secondary cell walls that provide structural support), which can be formed from parenchymatic precursor cells.
evidence: Based on established knowledge of fiber cell differentiation.

claim: The transition between the early phase and the xylem expansion phase is triggered by the onset of flowering.
source: It has been shown that the transition between the early phase and the xylem expansion phase is triggered by the onset of flowering (Sibout et al., 2008), through a mobile shoot-derived signal, the plant hormone gibberellin (Ragni et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citations to Sibout et al., 2008 and Ragni et al., 2011.

claim: The transition between early phase and xylem expansion phase is mediated by the plant hormone gibberellin.
source: It has been shown that the transition between the early phase and the xylem expansion phase is triggered by the onset of flowering (Sibout et al., 2008), through a mobile shoot-derived signal, the plant hormone gibberellin (Ragni et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citation to Ragni et al., 2011.

claim: The study analyzed two Arabidopsis accessions: Columbia-0 (Col-0) and Landsberg erecta (Ler).
source: For analysis we chose two common laboratory accessions, Columbia-0 (Col-0) and Landsberg erecta (Ler), which have already been shown to display divergent secondary growth dynamics (Ragni et al., 2011).
evidence: Explicitly stated in the text with citation to Ragni et al., 2011.

claim: Col-0 and Ler have been shown to display divergent secondary growth dynamics.
source: For analysis we chose two common laboratory accessions, Columbia-0 (Col-0) and Landsberg erecta (Ler), which have already been shown to display divergent secondary growth dynamics (Ragni et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citation to Ragni et al., 2011.

claim: The study analyzed five time points: 15, 20, 25, 30, and 35 days after germination (dag).
source: Based on the secondary growth progression observed during pilot experiments, we chose to analyze five time points in detail, starting at 15 days after germination (dag), when a full cambium is established and the initial outer epidermal and cortex cell layers are already or about to be shed. This was followed by additional sampling at 20, 25, 30 and up to 35 dag, when the plants had seized formation of new flowers (Figure 1B).
evidence: Explicitly stated in text and shown in Figure 1B.

claim: At 15 dag, a full cambium is established and the initial outer epidermal and cortex cell layers are already or about to be shed.
source: Based on the secondary growth progression observed during pilot experiments, we chose to analyze five time points in detail, starting at 15 days after germination (dag), when a full cambium is established and the initial outer epidermal and cortex cell layers are already or about to be shed.
evidence: Based on observations from pilot experiments.

claim: Plants were grown in soil in a 16 hr light–8 hr dark cycle at 22°C with 150 µE light intensity.
source: Plants were grown in soil in a 16 hr light–8 hr dark cycle at 22°C with 150 µE light intensity.
evidence: Explicitly stated experimental conditions.

claim: All plants of both genotypes flowered at 17 dag ±1 d under the experimental conditions.
source: In our conditions, all plants of both genotypes flowered at 17 dag ±1 d.
evidence: Experimental observation reported in the study.

claim: The average hypocotyl stele diameter was ca. 0.3 mm in Col-0 and ca. 0.15 mm in Ler at 15 dag.
source: Whereas the average hypocotyl stele diameter was ca. 0.3 mm in Col-0 and ca. 0.15 mm in Ler at 15 dag, the radial expansion resulted in an average diameter of 1.6 mm in Col-0 and 1.1 mm in Ler at 35 dag.
evidence: Measurements from the study's data.

claim: The radial expansion resulted in an average diameter of 1.6 mm in Col-0 and 1.1 mm in Ler at 35 dag.
source: Whereas the average hypocotyl stele diameter was ca. 0.3 mm in Col-0 and ca. 0.15 mm in Ler at 15 dag, the radial expansion resulted in an average diameter of 1.6 mm in Col-0 and 1.1 mm in Ler at 35 dag.
evidence: Measurements from the study's data.

claim: Relative xylem area increased from 12% to 29% in Col-0 between 15 and 35 dag.
source: Concomitantly, relative xylem area increased from 12% to 29% in Col-0, and from 31% to 47% in Ler, confirming previous observations (Ragni et al., 2011).
evidence: Measurements from the study's data, confirmed by citation to Ragni et al., 2011.

claim: Relative xylem area increased from 31% to 47% in Ler between 15 and 35 dag.
source: Concomitantly, relative xylem area increased from 12% to 29% in Col-0, and from 31% to 47% in Ler, confirming previous observations (Ragni et al., 2011).
evidence: Measurements from the study's data, confirmed by citation to Ragni et al., 2011.

claim: The study used plastic resin embedding to acquire 3 µm thin cross-sections while conserving cellular structure.
source: Embedding was performed using plastic resin, which proved to be the only robust method to acquire 3 µm thin cross-sections while conserving the cellular structure.
evidence: Methodological observation from the study.

claim: Images were obtained at 40X magnification with a resolution of 1024 × 1024 pixels.
source: Our strategy was to produce ultra-high resolution images of 1024 × 1024 pixels, which would allow a very fine discrimination of individual cell boundaries, the critical requirement for the subsequent image segmentation process.
evidence: Methodological detail from the study.

claim: Individual cross section images were assembled from a minimum of 9 (3 × 3) up to 144 (12 × 12) panels.
source: Individual cross section images subjected to segmentation were thus assembled from a minimum of 9 (3 × 3) up to 144 (12 × 12) panels (Figure 1C).
evidence: Methodological detail from the study, illustrated in Figure 1C.

claim: The automated image processing and segmentation pipeline performed at more than 99% accuracy.
source: The pipeline is fully automated and robust and typically performed at more than 99% accuracy (i.e., less than 1% of mis-segmented cells) across the scale of images (Figure 1F).
evidence: Performance metric from the study, illustrated in Figure 1F.

claim: CPU time for image processing scaled exponentially with image size, taking ca. 8 min for a 15 dag sample but ca. 1000 min for a 35 dag sample.
source: However, because CPU time scaled exponentially with image size, taking ca. 8 min. for a 15 dag sample but ca. 1000 min for a 35 dag sample, computation eventually became limiting for our endeavor.
evidence: Computational performance observation from the study.

claim: The study analyzed ca. 20 selected cross sections per genotype and time point (208 cross sections in total).
source: Thus, we restricted our analysis to ca. 20 selected cross sections per genotype and time point (i.e., 208 cross sections in total, requiring ca. 800 hr of total CPU time) (Figure 1B), which gave statistically robust quantitative data.
evidence: Methodological detail from the study, shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Overall median cell number at 15 dag was 883 for Col-0 and 260 for Ler.
source: Overall median cell number at 15 dag was 883 for Col-0 and 260 for Ler.
evidence: Quantitative measurement from the study's data.

claim: At 35 dag, median cell number had increased to 18,124 for Col-0 and 11,026 for Ler.
source: At 35 dag, it had increased to 18'124 and 11'026, respectively, indicating higher overall secondary growth in Col-0, but higher relative secondary growth in Ler (i.e., a ca. 42-fold vs a ca. 21-fold increase in cell number).
evidence: Quantitative measurement from the study's data.

claim: Col-0 showed higher overall secondary growth than Ler, but Ler showed higher relative secondary growth (ca. 42-fold vs ca. 21-fold increase in cell number).
source: At 35 dag, it had increased to 18'124 and 11'026, respectively, indicating higher overall secondary growth in Col-0, but higher relative secondary growth in Ler (i.e., a ca. 42-fold vs a ca. 21-fold increase in cell number).
evidence: Inference from quantitative measurements in the study.

claim: Total transverse area increased from ca. 70,000 µm² at 15 dag to ca. 2 million µm² at 35 dag in Col-0.
source: Together with the overall increase in total transverse area (from ca. 70'000 µm2 at 15 dag to ca. 2 million µm2 at 35 dag and ca. 11'000 µm2 to ca. 1 million µm2 for Col-0 and Ler, respectively), this suggests significantly different secondary growth dynamics in the two genotypes.
evidence: Quantitative measurement from the study's data.

claim: Total transverse area increased from ca. 11,000 µm² at 15 dag to ca. 1 million µm² at 35 dag in Ler.
source: Together with the overall increase in total transverse area (from ca. 70'000 µm2 at 15 dag to ca. 2 million µm2 at 35 dag and ca. 11'000 µm2 to ca. 1 million µm2 for Col-0 and Ler, respectively), this suggests significantly different secondary growth dynamics in the two genotypes.
evidence: Quantitative measurement from the study's data.

claim: The study computed 16 cellular descriptors representing geometric characteristics of cell shape and relative cell position.
source: Thus, we advanced towards our goal of a full cellular resolution analysis by computing 16 cellular descriptors that represent the geometric characteristics of cell shape and relative cell position (Supplementary file 1A).
evidence: Methodological detail from the study.

claim: The study used support vector machine (SVM) algorithm for automated cell type recognition.
source: To overcome this limitation, we sought to develop automated cell type recognition that uses the descriptors as an input for cell type classification. To this end, we performed a supervised classification using the support vector machine algorithm (SVM) (Cortes and Vapnik, 1995).
evidence: Methodological approach with citation to Cortes and Vapnik, 1995.

claim: The training set comprised a total of 3,144 manually labeled cells.
source: The training set was a subset of our data that comprised a total of 3'144 manually labeled cells, dispatched into two sections per time point and genotype (Supplementary file 1B).
evidence: Methodological detail from the study.

claim: Five distinct cell type categories could be classified: (i) xylem vessels and parenchymatic cells, (ii) xylem fibers, (iii) cambial cells, (iv) phloem bundle cells, and (v) parenchymatic phloem cells.
source: Across all sections and time points, a common set of five distinct cell type categories (Supplementary file 1D) could be classified and quantified, that is (i) xylem vessels and parenchymatic cells, (ii) xylem fibers, (iii) cambial cells, (iv) phloem bundle cells (companion cells and sieve elements) and (v) parenchymatic phloem cells (including any of the rare phloem fibers) (Supplementary file 1E).
evidence: Methodological outcome from the study.

claim: The automated cell type recognition achieved an average accuracy of 88% and a median accuracy of 95%.
source: For these categories, our purely morphology- and position-based approach identified cells with an average accuracy of 88% and a median accuracy of 95% across the n = 50 cell type category X time point X genotype matrix.
evidence: Performance metric from the study.

claim: Xylem vessel and parenchyma cell recognition had lower accuracy especially at later stages, frequently confused with phloem parenchyma cells.
source: Whereas the automated recognition with these classifiers was thus sufficiently accurate for most cell type categories to extract quantitative data about secondary growth progression from the typically thousands of cells per section, the recognition of the xylem vessel and parenchyma cells behaved as an outlier, with lower accuracy especially at later stages. We also noticed that xylem cell types were frequently assigned to cells outside of the xylem area's average radius. This was particularly prevalent at the later stages of development and could be pinpointed to a frequent confusion between xylem vessels and phloem parenchyma cells, which increasingly resemble each other in their outlines as secondary growth proceeds.
evidence: Observation from the study's analysis.

claim: The automated quality control pipeline corrected mis-assigned xylem cell identities using mask-defined xylem areas.
source: The tool also automatically corrected the mis-assigned xylem cell identities by taking advantage of the mask-defined xylem area of the quality control filter. This correction refined the cell type recognition results and permitted all sections to pass the filtering step.
evidence: Methodological detail from the study.

claim: Principal component analysis revealed that the first two principal components explained 76% of the variation.
source: The computed correlation matrix was projected into a two-dimensional coordinate system, with the first two principal components explaining 76% of the variation.
evidence: Statistical analysis result from the study.

claim: The phenoprint clustering suggests a conserved sequence of development from one distinct morphological pattern to another, albeit with different temporal progression in Col-0 vs Ler.
source: Overall, the phenoprint clustering suggests a conserved sequence of development from one distinct morphological pattern to another, albeit with a different temporal progression in Col-0 vs Ler.
evidence: Inference from principal component analysis results.

claim: Ler has a higher ratio of xylem area to phloem area than most other accessions, including Col-0.
source: Previous studies (Ragni et al., 2011) have shown that Ler has a higher ratio of xylem area to phloem area than most other accessions, including Col-0.
evidence: Supported by citation to Ragni et al., 2011.

claim: Overall radial expansion of Ler was reduced as compared to Col-0.
source: Our quantification also confirmed that overall radial expansion of Ler was reduced as compared to Col-0 (Figure 3B).
evidence: Quantitative measurement from the study, shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Xylem area expansion rate was nearly equal in both genotypes.
source: However, xylem area expansion rate was nearly equal in both genotypes, which combined with lower overall radial expansion necessarily resulted in higher xylem occupancy in Ler (Figure 3C).
evidence: Quantitative measurement from the study, shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Two distinct phases of xylem occupancy could be distinguished: initially it decreased or remained stable between 15 and 25 dag, followed by an increase between 25 and 35 dag.
source: In the temporal trend, two distinct phases of xylem occupancy could be distinguished. Initially, it decreased or remained stable between 15 and 25 dag, followed by an increase between 25 and 35 dag.
evidence: Observation from temporal analysis of the data.

claim: Ler's xylem area increased steadily, eventually occupying almost 50% of the total transverse area at 35 dag.
source: Whereas these tendencies were similar in both genotypes up to 30 dag, Ler differed in that its xylem area increased steadily, eventually occupying almost 50% of the total transverse area at 35 dag.
evidence: Quantitative measurement from the study.

claim: The number of xylem cells and the xylem cell proliferation rate were close in both genotypes.
source: Quantification of cell proliferation confirmed that the number of xylem cells and the xylem cell proliferation rate were close in both genotypes (Figure 3D), however the total number of cells in Ler was ca. twofold lower than in Col-0 (Figure 3E).
evidence: Quantitative measurement from the study, shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The total number of cells in Ler was ca. twofold lower than in Col-0.
source: Quantification of cell proliferation confirmed that the number of xylem cells and the xylem cell proliferation rate were close in both genotypes (Figure 3D), however the total number of cells in Ler was ca. twofold lower than in Col-0 (Figure 3E).
evidence: Quantitative measurement from the study, shown in Figure 3E.

claim: The phloem proliferation rate was more than twofold lower in Ler, with stagnation in phloem cell number between 30 and 35 dag.
source: Moreover, the phloem proliferation rate was more than twofold lower in Ler, with stagnation in phloem cell number between 30 and 35 dag (Figure 3D) explaining the high xylem tissue occupancy at 35 dag.
evidence: Quantitative measurement from the study, shown in Figure 3D.

claim: A plateau in cambial growth combined with stagnating phloem proliferation is responsible for overall reduced radial growth but relatively increased xylem expansion in Ler.
source: In summary, our results suggest that a plateau in cambial growth combined with stagnating phloem proliferation is responsible for overall reduced radial growth but relatively increased xylem expansion in Ler.
evidence: Inference from the quantitative measurements and analysis.

claim: The incline angle represents the deviation of the major axis of a cell with respect to the radius emanating from the manually defined center point of the cross section.
source: The incline angle represents the deviation of the major axis of a cell with respect to the radius emanating from the manually defined center point of the cross section (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Definition provided in the study, illustrated in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: A value of zero for incline angle represents perfectly orthoradial (tangential or periclinal) orientation of the major axis.
source: A value of zero represents perfectly orthoradial (i.e., tangential or periclinal) orientation of the major axis, and a value of π/2 represents perfectly radial (i.e., anticlinal) orientation.
evidence: Definition provided in the study.

claim: A value of π/2 for incline angle represents perfectly radial (anticlinal) orientation.
source: A value of zero represents perfectly orthoradial (i.e., tangential or periclinal) orientation of the major axis, and a value of π/2 represents perfectly radial (i.e., anticlinal) orientation.
evidence: Definition provided in the study.

claim: At 15 dag in Col-0, the incline angle was uniformly distributed, meaning no distinguishable vascular organization of cell orientation was yet built up.
source: This could be visualized in violin plots (Figure 4C–D), where the incline angle was uniformly distributed at 15 dag in Col-0 (Hartigans' dip test p>10−3), meaning that no distinguishable vascular organization of cell orientation was yet built up.
evidence: Statistical analysis result from the study, shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Starting at 20 dag in Col-0, a first peak towards lower values of incline emerged and persisted until 35 dag.
source: Starting at 20 dag, a first peak towards lower values of incline emerged and persisted until 35 dag.
evidence: Observation from temporal analysis of incline angle distribution.

claim: At 30 dag in Col-0, a second peak towards higher values of incline arose, giving shape to a discernable bimodal distribution.
source: At 30 dag, a second peak towards higher values of incline arose, giving shape to a discernable bimodal distribution (Hartigans' dip test p<2.2 × 10−6) (Figure 4C).
evidence: Statistical analysis result from the study, shown in Figure 4C.

claim: In Ler at later time points (25-35 dag), sharp bimodal-shaped density curves supported the coexistence of two populations of cells, a mostly radially and a mostly orthoradially oriented one.
source: At the later time points, sharp bimodal-shaped density curves supported the coexistence of two populations of cells, a mostly radially and a mostly orthoradially oriented one (Hartigans' dip test p<2.2 × 10−6), similar to Col-0.
evidence: Statistical analysis result from the study.

claim: At 15 dag in Col-0, a wavy line described the point cloud of incline vs radial position, meaning that a radial vs orthoradial tissue boundary was not yet distinguishable.
source: In Col-0, the spatial distribution of the cell incline displayed unexpected temporal dynamics. At 15 dag, a wavy line described the point cloud, meaning that a radial vs orthoradial tissue boundary was not yet distinguishable (Figure 5A).
evidence: Observation from spatial analysis, shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Around 20 and 25 dag in Col-0, vascular organization emerged as a plateau of largely radial orientation close to the center corresponding to xylem cells, followed by a steep decrease to lower incline values in the cambium and phloem tissues.
source: However, around 20 and 25 dag, vascular organization emerged as a plateau of largely radial orientation close to the center that corresponded to xylem cells, followed by a steep decrease to lower incline values in the cambium and phloem tissues (Figure 5C,E).
evidence: Observation from spatial analysis, shown in Figures 5C and 5E.

claim: Once vascular organization was established, the plateau of xylem enlarged while the span of the orthoradial cell layers narrowed, concomitant with the occurrence of xylem fibers and expansion of the xylem area.
source: Once this pattern was established, the plateau of xylem enlarged while the span of the orthoradial cell layers narrowed, concomitant with the occurrence of xylem fibers and expansion of the xylem area (Figure 5G,I).
evidence: Observation from temporal analysis, shown in Figures 5G and 5I.

claim: A decrease in the variation spread of incline in cambial cells over time reflected the progressive enlargement and organization of the cambium.
source: We also observed a decrease in the variation spread of incline in cambial cells over time. This reflected the progressive enlargement and organization of the cambium, which appeared to be completed as late as 30 dag, confirming continuous refinement of vascular patterning during secondary growth.
evidence: Observation and inference from temporal analysis.

claim: The progressive enlargement and organization of the cambium appeared to be completed as late as 30 dag.
source: We also observed a decrease in the variation spread of incline in cambial cells over time. This reflected the progressive enlargement and organization of the cambium, which appeared to be completed as late as 30 dag, confirming continuous refinement of vascular patterning during secondary growth.
evidence: Observation from temporal analysis.

claim: Practically no post-cambial cell divisions were observed in the xylem area.
source: Visual inspection of cross sections suggested that this is not the case however, also revealing a remarkable rarity of post-cambial cell divisions. In the xylem area, practically no post-cambial divisions were observed (Figure 5—figure supplement 1) and radial cell files were generally continuous with the adjacent cambial files.
evidence: Observation from visual inspection, shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Radial cell files in xylem were generally continuous with the adjacent cambial files.
source: In the xylem area, practically no post-cambial divisions were observed (Figure 5—figure supplement 1) and radial cell files were generally continuous with the adjacent cambial files.
evidence: Observation from visual inspection.

claim: Cellular growth in xylem led to a switch from orthoradial to radial orientation in cell incline angle.
source: Following such cell files also suggested that cellular growth led to a switch in xylem cell incline angle orientation. Whereas xylem cells that emerged from the cambium still retained the orthoradial orientation, cellular growth eventually resulted in a switch towards a radial orientation.
evidence: Observation from visual inspection and analysis.

claim: Switching from orthoradial to radial orientation was not observed in the phloem.
source: Such switching was not observed in the phloem, consistent with the prevalence of orthoradial inclines.
evidence: Observation from visual inspection and analysis.

claim: Phloem cells were typically in continuity with the corresponding cambial cell files, and practically no cell divisions were observed in phloem parenchyma.
source: Similar to the xylem however, phloem cells were typically in continuity with the corresponding cambial cell files, and practically no cell divisions, neither anticlinal nor periclinal, were observed.
evidence: Observation from visual inspection.

claim: In cell files that ended up in vascular bundles, numerous post-cambial divisions could be observed, both in the anticlinal and periclinal orientations.
source: The exceptions to this were cell files that ended up in vascular bundles. In these, numerous post-cambial divisions could be observed, both in the anticlinal and periclinal orientations.
evidence: Observation from visual inspection.

claim: The vast majority of cell divisions was observed in the cambium, mostly in a perfect periclinal orientation.
source: Finally, as expected the vast majority of cell divisions was observed in the cambium. Mostly, they occurred in a perfect periclinal orientation, but we also observed numerous interspersed anticlinal divisions that are necessary to keep up with overall radial expansion.
evidence: Observation from visual inspection.

claim: Numerous interspersed anticlinal divisions in the cambium are necessary to keep up with overall radial expansion.
source: Mostly, they occurred in a perfect periclinal orientation, but we also observed numerous interspersed anticlinal divisions that are necessary to keep up with overall radial expansion.
evidence: Observation and inference from visual inspection.

claim: The radial expansion of hypocotyls appeared to be mostly driven by cambial activity and very little by post-cambial cell divisions.
source: In summary, the radial expansion of hypocotyls appeared to be mostly driven by cambial activity and very little by post-cambial cell divisions.
evidence: Summary inference from observations of cell division patterns.

claim: The patterning of phloem pole position might already be laid down in the cambium.
source: Since there appeared to be no cessation of cell division in the cell files connecting the cambium and the vascular bundles, the data suggested that the patterning of phloem pole position might already be laid down in the cambium.
evidence: Inference from observations of cell division patterns.

claim: Statistical analysis of emerging phloem poles revealed their spacing with a constant arc interspace distance.
source: Statistical analysis of the position of emerging phloem poles around the cambium revealed their spacing with a constant arc interspace distance.
evidence: Statistical analysis result from the study.

claim: The distance between emerging phloem poles remains constant over time as the cambial circumference enlarges.
source: That is, the distance between emerging phloem poles remains constant over time as the cambial circumference enlarges.
evidence: Observation from statistical analysis.

claim: The constant arc interspace distance between phloem poles has a span of ca. 140 μm.
source: This was revealed by determination of the corresponding probability density function for the distance between the spikes by an automated Bayesian model (Granqvist et al., 2012), which indicates a constant arc interspace distance (Figure 6C) with a span of ca. 140 μm, suggesting that vascular bundle formation is a patterned rather than a stochastic process.
evidence: Statistical analysis result using Bayesian model, shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Vascular bundle formation is a patterned rather than a stochastic process.
source: This was revealed by determination of the corresponding probability density function for the distance between the spikes by an automated Bayesian model (Granqvist et al., 2012), which indicates a constant arc interspace distance (Figure 6C) with a span of ca. 140 μm, suggesting that vascular bundle formation is a patterned rather than a stochastic process.
evidence: Inference from statistical analysis of phloem pole spacing.

claim: A reaction-diffusion model with a growing boundary would be consistent with the constant arc interspace distance for phloem pole formation.
source: A reaction-diffusion model with a growing boundary (i.e., representing the expanding xylem area) would be consistent with these results.
evidence: Theoretical speculation based on the observed pattern.

claim: The growing xylem area might exert a compression force on surrounding cambial and parenchymal cells, forcing them into tangential anisotropic cell elongation.
source: One possible explanation for this phenomenon could be tissue mechanics. The growing xylem area might exert a compression force on surrounding cambial and parenchymal cells, forcing them into tangential anisotropic cell elongation.
evidence: Speculative explanation for observed cell orientation patterns.

claim: A receptor-like kinase—peptide ligand pair is involved in cambial polarity and interacts with hormone signaling pathways.
source: A receptor-like kinase—peptide ligand pair is involved in this process and interacts with hormone signaling pathways (Hirakawa et al., 2008, 2010; Etchells et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citations to Hirakawa et al., 2008, 2010 and Etchells et al., 2012.

claim: The phenotypic penetrance of cambial polarity mutants is background-dependent, with stronger effects in Ler than in Col-0.
source: Notably, the phenotypic penetrance of the respective mutants is background-dependent, with stronger effects in Ler than in Col-0 (Etchells et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to Etchells et al., 2013.

claim: Initial secondary growth appears to be particularly slow in Ler as indicated by more than threefold difference in cell number at 15 dag compared to Col-0.
source: Rather, initial secondary growth appears to be particularly slow in Ler as indicated by more than threefold difference in cell number at 15 dag.
evidence: Inference from quantitative measurements.

claim: Between 15 dag and 25 dag, Ler shows an acceleration of cell production that surpasses Col-0 in relative terms.
source: This is followed by an acceleration of cell production that surpasses Col-0 in relative terms between 15 dag and 25 dag, before dropping to Col-0 levels between 25 dag and 35 dag.
evidence: Observation from temporal analysis of cell production rates.

claim: The quantitative histology approach along a series of time points revealed highly divergent secondary growth dynamics in the genotypes that would not have been evident from a comparison of end points.
source: Thus, our analysis along a series of time points has revealed highly divergent secondary growth dynamics in the genotypes that would not have been evident from a comparison of end points.
evidence: Inference from temporal analysis comparing the two genotypes.
